ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, pruritic, erythematous plaque on the eyelid with lymphocytic infiltrates and atypical lymphocytes
salient_findings: pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
key_facts: 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules
no remarkable medical history
routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
histopathologic examination revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates
exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
focal mild follicular mucin deposition on Alcian blue staining
lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, pruritic, erythematous plaque with lymphocytic infiltrates and atypical lymphocytes, consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: CD4-positive lymphocytic infiltrates and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, suggesting a CD4+ T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, although lack of systemic symptoms and normal blood tests make it less likely

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lesions and lymphocytic infiltrates, but the presence of atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement suggests a more aggressive lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, pruritic, erythematous plaque with lymphocytic infiltrates and atypical lymphocytes, consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a pruritic, dark red plaque with perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes, and a CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1, along with monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, are characteristic features of mycosis fungoides

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific features distinguishing it from mycosis fungoides in this case

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Typically involves widespread skin lesions and lymphadenopathy, not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Characterized by papular lesions that ulcerate and crust, not matching the plaque description

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as mycosis fungoides is a specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
